record.final_answer:
Achievable, but not with the setup you almost certainly have today — and the cheap fix (turn down the poll interval) does not get you there.

What the Nimbrel docs say (SDK 4.x, read 2026-04-20):

- Default behaviour is polling every 30s, and the polling interval cannot be set below 10s. So a flip can take up to ~30s to land as-is, and the theoretical floor for polling is 10s — 5s is unreachable by polling alone, no matter how you tune it.
- Sub-5s requires push: `stream: true` in the SDK client options, which delivers rule changes over a stream instead of on a timer. That is gated to the Team plan or above.

What it would take:

1. Confirm the plan tier. If you're below Team, this is a commercial change, not an engineering one — nothing else on this list matters until that's resolved.
2. Confirm every running service is on SDK 4.x and actually passes `stream: true` in its client options. Client options are read at construction, so this needs one deploy/restart per service to take effect.
3. Make sure each service re-reads the flag on the push callback. A stream update that lands in an SDK cache nobody consults is indistinguishable from no update — services that snapshot config at startup or hold flags in a long-lived struct need a wiring change too.
4. Keep polling as a fallback so a dropped stream degrades to the 30s path rather than freezing flags at their last value.
5. Instrument it: log receipt time per service and measure flip-to-effect, plus alert on stream disconnects. Without that, you can't honestly tell Product you meet 5s — you'd only be claiming it.

Two caveats worth saying to Product before committing:

- 5s with push is a typical-case number, not a guaranteed bound. Stream reconnect, SDK caching, and service-side re-read all add variance; promising a hard 5s SLA needs the monitoring in step 5 to back it.
- The source note is from April 2026 against 4.x. Re-check the current docs (docs.nimbrel.example/sdk/updates) for stream support and plan gating before you quote it as a commitment.

So: yes on Team plan+ and SDK 4.x with streaming wired through every service and a restart to apply it; no if you're staying on polling or below Team.
